engine: Chatterbox-Nano (Resemble AI, 110M, English) - 2026 release, loaded via ChatterboxTurboTTS(nano=True)
latest_version: Checkpoint t3_nano_v1.safetensors in HF repo ResembleAI/chatterbox-nano (repo created 2026-04-14, announced 2026-07-06, last modified 2026-07-21). Code support landed in GitHub master on 2026-07-21 (commit 5de7a54, PR #542); master HEAD is ab55923c27757c90cfcc407baa57dc25a7d25217 (2026-11-04, README-only). NOT on PyPI: chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 (2026-03-26) predates Nano. README notice: 'As of August 2026, Chatterbox is retired research and is no longer maintained.'
code_license: MIT (LICENSE file in resemble-ai/chatterbox, GitHub SPDX: MIT)
weights_license: MIT (HF model card front-matter 'license: mit', tag license:mit on ResembleAI/chatterbox-nano)
commercial_notes: MIT on both code and weights, so monetized YouTube voice-over is allowed. Every output carries Resemble's imperceptible PerTh watermark (applied in generate()). Clone only your own voice or one you have consent for. The README says the code 'stays public as an archive under the MIT license' with no support.
params: Marketed as 110M. Checkpoint headers read today: t3_nano_v1 = 217.5M F32 params (GPT2-small backbone 130M incl. a 38.6M word-embedding table deleted at load, plus text emb/head); shared s3gen_meanflow decoder = 266.1M F32; voice encoder 1.4M. About 445M params live in memory.
download_size_gb: 3.0 GB via from_pretrained (snapshot_download of *.safetensors pulls an unused 1.06 GB s3gen.safetensors; about 1.94 GB is actually loaded). Plus Python packages: torch 2.6.0+cu124 wheel is a 2.53 GB download, or 0.21 GB for the CPU-only wheel.
vram_gb_min: Not measured on any 4 GB card (no report found). Estimate from fp32 weights: 1.78 GB of weights on device + CUDA context + activations = roughly 2.2-2.5 GB. Measured CPU peak RSS is 2.55 GB (Windows 11 test). So it should fit a 4 GB card when about 2.5 GB is free, but NOT in the ~1.4 GB free while the desktop is busy. All checkpoints are F32 and the source has no autocast/.half(), so default inference is fp32 (safe for GTX 16xx).
speed_note: CPU, official loader, fp32, warm: RTF 1.83 (6 threads) / 1.93 (12 threads) on Ryzen 5 5625U, torch 2.6.0 CPU (socialvik.com, 2026-10-16). RTF 1.65-2.6 warm on Ryzen 5 4600H under Windows 11, first call cold RTF 6-10, model load 5-9 s (github.com/Rohan0603/daemon-reborn issue #27, 2026-11-04/07). So expect about 1.5-2x slower than realtime on a Ryzen 5 5600H (my extrapolation). Resemble's '3x faster than realtime on 8 CPU cores' (RTF 0.33) was not reproduced by either. Vendor GPU claim: 10x realtime (blog, GPU unnamed). No GTX 1650 figure found.
python_versions: requires-python >=3.10; developed/tested on Python 3.11 (Debian 11). Pins cover 3.10-3.13 with torch 2.6.0; 3.14 needs torch>=2.9. Use 3.11.
windows_install:
Not executed by me; assembled from pyproject.toml, the PyTorch wheel index and issue reports. Use a dedicated venv (hard pins clash with other engines).
1) uv venv --python 3.11 --seed
2) GPU: uv pip install torch==2.6.0 torchaudio==2.6.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 (torch-2.6.0+cu124-cp311-cp311-win_amd64.whl verified to exist, 2.53 GB). CPU-only: same with .../whl/cpu (0.21 GB). Plain PyPI torch==2.6.0 on Windows is CPU-only.
3) uv pip install "chatterbox-tts @ git+https://github.com/resemble-ai/chatterbox.git@ab55923c27757c90cfcc407baa57dc25a7d25217" (needs Git for Windows; master also pulls resemble-perth from git master, v1.1.0, commit ff1c8ac). Do NOT use 'pip install chatterbox-tts' for Nano: PyPI 0.1.7 raises unexpected keyword 'nano'.
Pinned deps: transformers==5.2.0, diffusers==0.29.0, numpy>=1.24,<2, librosa==0.11.0, safetensors==0.5.3, conformer==0.3.2, pykakasi==2.3.0, gradio==6.8.0, s3tokenizer, spacy-pkuseg (win_amd64 cp311 wheel exists), pyloudnorm, omegaconf.
Blockers: none of pynini/triton/deepspeed/flash-attn. Known trap: PyPI resemble-perth 1.0.1 imports pkg_resources, so in a uv venv PerthImplicitWatermarker is None and loading fails with "TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable"; fix is the git install above or adding "setuptools<81" (the Windows 11 test pinned it). Pass device as the string "cpu"/"cuda", not torch.device (issue #533).
instruct_on_cloned_voice: No free-text instruction. Partial: inline paralinguistic tags in the script text work with a cloned reference. exaggeration and cfg_weight are accepted but ignored with a warning (source: 'CFG, min_p and exaggeration are not supported by the Nano version and will be ignored').
emotion_controls: Tags only. Officially supported (Resemble staff on HF, EVENT_TAGS in gradio_tts_turbo_app.py): [clear throat] [sigh] [shush] [cough] [groan] [sniff] [gasp] [chuckle] [laugh]. The Turbo tokenizer also has 10 undocumented style tokens ([angry] [fear] [surprised] [whispering] [advertisement] [dramatic] [narration] [crying] [happy] [sarcastic]); user reports conflict on whether they do anything (issue #557 vs #492). Sampling knobs: temperature 0.8, top_k 1000, top_p 0.95, repetition_penalty 1.2, norm_loudness. No seed argument; call torch.manual_seed() first (as the Gradio app does).
speed_control: None. No speed/rate parameter in generate(); a request for slower speech on the Turbo HF page is unanswered. Time-stretch in post if needed.
minimal_python_usage:
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts_turbo import ChatterboxTurboTTS

model = ChatterboxTurboTTS.from_pretrained(device="cpu", nano=True)  # or device="cuda"
wav = model.generate("Your sentence here.", audio_prompt_path="your_10s_ref_clip.wav")
ta.save("test-nano.wav", wav, model.sr)  # 24 kHz mono

# Sentence-by-sentence: call model.prepare_conditionals("ref.wav") once, then model.generate(sentence) without audio_prompt_path (passing the path re-encodes the reference every call).
cloning_quality_note: No independent listening test or similarity score for Nano's cloning was found. The one independent CPU write-up (socialvik) timed only the built-in voice and explicitly did not score quality; the Windows validation log lists human listening as NOT RUN. Resemble gives no WER/similarity numbers for Nano. Quality on your voice is unknown until you A/B it; expect it to be below Turbo given the smaller backbone.
known_issues: Project is retired and unmaintained (383 open issues, fixes unmerged). Not installable from PyPI. Shares Turbo's limits: 1000 speech tokens (40 s) per call, reference must be longer than 5 s and only the first 10-15 s is used, no pause tag, tags are hit-or-miss. Vendor CPU speed claim not reproduced. Mutable git dependency on Perth master. Watermark always on.
verdict_reason: The only Chatterbox variant with evidence of running acceptably on this class of machine: installed and run on Windows 11 on a 6-core Ryzen laptop CPU at roughly 2x slower than realtime with 2.5 GB RAM, fp32 throughout, MIT weights, 3 GB download. Needs no transcript. Cloning quality is unverified, so it must be A/B tested; it has no exaggeration/cfg or free-text style control.

latest_version: Checkpoint t3_turbo_v1.safetensors in HF repo ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo (created 2025-12-02, last modified 2025-12-15). Shipped in PyPI chatterbox-tts 0.1.5 (2025-12-12) / 0.1.6 (2025-12-15); latest PyPI is 0.1.7 (2026-03-26). No newer Turbo checkpoint in 2026. Project marked retired/unmaintained as of August 2026 (README notice committed 2026-11-04).
weights_license: MIT (HF model card 'License: mit', tag license:mit on ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo)
commercial_notes: MIT code and weights; monetized YouTube use is allowed. PerTh watermark is embedded in every output. Use your own or a consented reference voice.
params: Marketed as 350M. Headers read today: t3_turbo_v1 = 478.9M F32 (GPT2-medium backbone 362M incl. a 51.5M embedding table deleted at load); s3gen_meanflow = 266.1M F32; voice encoder 1.4M. About 693M params live.
download_size_gb: 4.04 GB via from_pretrained (includes an unused 1.06 GB s3gen.safetensors; about 2.98 GB is loaded). Same Python packages as Nano.
vram_gb_min: No measurement on a 4 GB card found. fp32 weights on device = 2.77 GB, so estimated peak about 3.2-3.6 GB. Secondary user reports quote 4.5-5 GB on unnamed (larger) GPUs. NVIDIA's NVIGI/ggml build lists about 2.3 GB, but that is a different runtime and precision. Default PyTorch path is fp32 (no autocast/half in source).
speed_note: CPU: RTF 5.39 on Ryzen 5 5625U, 12 threads, torch 2.6.0 CPU, fp32 (socialvik.com, 2026-10-16), i.e. about 5 h 23 min per hour of audio; expect roughly 4-5x slower than realtime on a 5600H (my extrapolation). Picovoice (a competitor) measured 48 s time-to-audio and 7.5 GB peak RAM on a Ryzen 7 5700X. GPU: tts-bench as cited by yaps.ai got 1.1x realtime on an Apple M4. A separate ggml port (gsfjohnson/chatterbox.cpp, Q4_0, build from source) reports RTF 0.82 on a Ryzen 9 9950X. No GTX 1650 number found.
python_versions: requires-python >=3.10; tested by the authors on 3.11. Use 3.11.
windows_install:
Same environment as Nano (one install serves both). Turbo alone also works from PyPI:
1) uv venv --python 3.11 --seed
2) uv pip install torch==2.6.0 torchaudio==2.6.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 (or .../whl/cpu)
3) uv pip install chatterbox-tts==0.1.7 "setuptools<81" (setuptools pin works around resemble-perth 1.0.1 importing pkg_resources) - or the git install shown under Nano.
No pynini/triton/deepspeed/flash-attn. Not executed by me.
instruct_on_cloned_voice: No free-text instruction. Partial: paralinguistic tags typed inline in the text apply to the cloned voice. exaggeration/cfg_weight are ignored with a warning; Resemble staff confirmed they were removed from Turbo (CFG for speed, exaggeration because it hurt naturalness) and said to use the original model if you want them.
emotion_controls: Inline tags: [clear throat] [sigh] [shush] [cough] [groan] [sniff] [gasp] [chuckle] [laugh] (official list). 10 more style tokens exist in added_tokens.json ([angry] [whispering] [narration] [dramatic] etc.) but are not listed as supported; reports conflict (worked under ONNX per one user in #492, no effect under mlx-audio per #557). Sampling: temperature 0.8, top_k 1000, top_p 0.95, repetition_penalty 1.2. Seed via torch.manual_seed().
minimal_python_usage:
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts_turbo import ChatterboxTurboTTS

model = ChatterboxTurboTTS.from_pretrained(device="cuda")  # or "cpu"
wav = model.generate("Text with a [chuckle] tag.", audio_prompt_path="your_10s_ref_clip.wav")
ta.save("test-turbo.wav", wav, model.sr)
cloning_quality_note: Evidence is mostly vendor-side: Podonos listening tests linked from the README compare Turbo with ElevenLabs Turbo v2.5, Cartesia Sonic 3 and VibeVoice 7B, but Podonos is acknowledged as a supporter, so not independent. Independent metric evidence exists for the 0.5B family rather than Turbo (see original entry). User reports: cloning described as good on short text; hallucination beyond about 350 characters (#424) and instability after 25-30 s (#543); mispronunciation when the reference is minutes long (keep under 1 min); tags hit-or-miss. Sentence-by-sentence generation avoids the length problems.
known_issues: Unmaintained. Garbles long inputs (>~350 chars / >25-30 s); hard cap 1000 speech tokens = 40 s. Double quotes can be voiced as a sigh sound (#433). No pause tag, no speed control, no exaggeration/cfg. Reference must be >5 s; only first 10-15 s used. Perth/setuptools load failure under uv. Watermark always on.
verdict_reason: MIT and installs cleanly on Windows, and it shares Nano's install so testing it costs only 4 GB of disk. But on this machine it is about 5x slower than realtime on CPU, and its roughly 3.2-3.6 GB fp32 footprint does not fit the 1.4 GB of free VRAM (it might fit only with the GPU otherwise empty, unverified). Worth an A/B against Nano only if you accept slow batch renders or can free the GPU.

engine: Chatterbox (original, 0.5B, English) - the variant with exaggeration + cfg_weight
latest_version: Checkpoint t3_cfg.safetensors + s3gen.safetensors in HF repo ResembleAI/chatterbox (repo created 2025-04-24; first PyPI release 0.1 on 2025-05-28). The English checkpoint has not been replaced; no 2026 update. Latest package: PyPI chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 (2026-03-26); GitHub master ab55923 (2026-11-04). Only GitHub release tag is v0.1.2 (2025-06-13). Retired/unmaintained since August 2026 per README.
weights_license: MIT (HF model card license 'mit', tag license:mit on ResembleAI/chatterbox)
commercial_notes: MIT code and weights. PerTh watermark in every output. A question on the HF page about commercial use of the demo reference voices is unanswered, so use your own reference clip.
params: 0.5B Llama backbone. Headers read today: t3_cfg = 532.4M F32, s3gen = 264.0M F32, voice encoder 1.4M; about 798M params total.
download_size_gb: 3.19 GB (from_pretrained fetches only ve.safetensors, t3_cfg.safetensors 2.13 GB, s3gen.safetensors 1.06 GB, tokenizer.json, conds.pt; the full HF repo is 13.87 GB but is not pulled).
vram_gb_min: fp32 weights alone are 3.19 GB, so over 3.6 GB before activations. Reports: about 5 GB on a GTX 1060 6 GB under Windows, with stalls when it hits the 6 GB limit (issue #508); maintainer relayed community reports of 6-7 GB (issue #44); about 5 GB on an RTX 3090 for the same-size Multilingual model. The roughly 1.5-2.5 GB figures need bfloat16/half-precision forks, which are not an option on a GTX 1650. Upstream has no fp16 path (issue #564: dtype mismatch errors).
speed_note: GPU: about 34-38 it/s in fp32 on a T4 and about 40 it/s on an RTX 4090 with master (issue #127; speech tokens are 25 Hz, so roughly 1.4-1.6x realtime for the token stage); about 5 s per typical sentence on a T4, streaming fork RTF 2.05 on a T4 (issue #193); about 15 s per sentence on a GTX 1060 6 GB (issue #508). CPU: no measured figure found for a 6-core laptop. It is heavier than Turbo (532M backbone, CFG doubles the batch, 10 decoder steps vs 2), and Turbo already measures RTF 5.39 on a Ryzen 5 5625U, so expect well beyond the 3x limit (my estimate: roughly 8-12x slower than realtime).
windows_install: Same package and steps as Turbo (PyPI chatterbox-tts==0.1.7 or git master; torch==2.6.0 from the cu124 or cpu index; "setuptools<81" if using PyPI resemble-perth). No compile-time blockers on Windows. Not executed by me.
instruct_on_cloned_voice: No free-text instruction and no tags. Partial via numeric knobs that DO apply to a cloned voice: exaggeration (emotion intensity, stored alongside the speaker embedding in the conditioning) and cfg_weight (pace/adherence).
emotion_controls: exaggeration: default 0.5, Gradio range 0.25-2 ('extreme values can be unstable'); cfg_weight: default 0.5, range 0-1. README tips: defaults suit most prompts; for a fast-talking reference lower cfg_weight to about 0.3; for dramatic delivery use cfg about 0.3 with exaggeration 0.7+. Also temperature 0.8, repetition_penalty 1.2, min_p 0.05, top_p 1.0. Seed via torch.manual_seed().
speed_control: No direct speed parameter. Indirect only: higher exaggeration speeds speech up, lower cfg_weight slows it down (README).
minimal_python_usage:
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS

model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cuda")  # or "cpu"
wav = model.generate("Your sentence.", audio_prompt_path="YOUR_FILE.wav", exaggeration=0.5, cfg_weight=0.5)
ta.save("test.wav", wav, model.sr)
cloning_quality_note: Independent metrics for the 0.5B family: soniqo.audio benchmark (July 2026, FLEURS English, 10 pairs, Chatterbox Multilingual fp16) gives speaker cosine 0.642 (third of 8, behind IndexTTS2 0.738 and F5-TTS 0.698; ahead of VoxCPM2, OmniVoice, Qwen3-TTS, Fish S2 Pro, Higgs), the best WER at 1.2%, but a low predicted-naturalness UTMOS of 2.22. Vendor numbers on Seed-TTS test-en (Flash card): SIM-o 0.685, WER 2.20, UTMOS 4.10. TTS Arena as reported by yaps.ai on 2026-10-10: Chatterbox #28 of 39, rating 1481, described as the highest clearly open-weight model, level with Kokoro (I could not load the leaderboard itself). A user moving from Qwen3-TTS (archy.net, March 2026) called English output clean and expressive with no seed pinning.
known_issues: Too large for this GPU in fp32. Occasional runaway generations and trailing hiss until the token limit (#508, #271); 1000-token (40 s) cap; skipped words reported (#408). Unmaintained. Perth/setuptools load failure under uv. Hard pins (transformers 5.2.0, gradio 6.8.0) need a dedicated venv.
verdict_reason: The only Chatterbox model whose emotion controls (exaggeration, cfg) work on a cloned voice, and it has the best independent quality evidence, MIT licensed. But 3.19 GB of fp32 weights will not fit the GTX 1650, and CPU speed is far outside the 3x limit. Install only if you want the exaggeration control enough to accept very slow CPU-only overnight renders; it reuses the same venv as Nano at a cost of 3.2 GB.
